starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The in-situ hard-rock pegmatite orebody where lithium is locked in spodumene (LiAlSi2O6). Anchored at the deposit itself, not the downstream concentrator or roaster.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Spodumene-bearing pegmatite ore (lithium hosted in spodumene; ~1-2% Li2O run-of-mine, upgradable to ~6% Li2O 'SC6' concentrate downstream)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Dominant hard-rock source globally (e.g., Australia, China, Zimbabwe, Canada). Spodumene is the only pegmatite mineral with reliable large-scale industrial Li production. Concentration and roast-leach are ROUTE steps, not the origin.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Deposit = origin; SC6 concentrate is a route intermediate.

starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium (principal or co-product); often co-hosted with Ta, Sn, feldspar/ceramic minerals
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The in-situ pegmatite orebody where lithium is hosted in petalite (LiAlSi4O10), amblygonite (LiAlPO4F), or eucryptite (LiAlSiO4) rather than spodumene. Anchored at the deposit.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Petalite/amblygonite/eucryptite-bearing pegmatite ore (lithium hosted in petalite ~3.0-4.7% Li2O, amblygonite/eucryptite ~10-12% Li2O)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Distinct mineral hosts within pegmatites; petalite widely used for glass/ceramics and produced commercially (e.g., Zimbabwe, Namibia, Australia). Amblygonite/eucryptite historically mined (Zimbabwe) but now minor. Different mineralogy/processing than spodumene warrants a separate group; kept distinct from mica-hosted lepidolite.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Could alternatively be folded into a single generic 'LCT pegmatite' group with SB-01; kept separate due to distinct ore mineralogy and processing routes.

starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Often companion to Sn-W, Cs, Rb, Ta systems; locally lithium-principal (e.g., Chinese lepidolite operations)
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The in-situ granite/pegmatite/greisen orebody where lithium is hosted in the mica minerals lepidolite (K(Li,Al)3(Si,Al)4O10(F,OH)2) or zinnwaldite (Fe-rich variety). Anchored at the deposit.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lepidolite/zinnwaldite mica ore (lithium hosted in lithium mica; lepidolite up to ~7.7% Li2O theoretical, zinnwaldite lower, Fe-rich)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Materially different mineralogy and processing (mica flotation, sulfate/chloride roasting, higher F/Rb/Cs impurity handling) than spodumene, so a separate group. Significant Chinese production; zinnwaldite associated with historic Sn-W greisen (e.g., Cinovec, Erzgebirge).
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Deposit = origin; mica concentrate is a route intermediate.

starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium (principal), often with potash, boron, magnesium co-products
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The subsurface closed-basin salar aquifer where lithium exists as dissolved Li+ in continental brine beneath salt flats. Anchored at the in-situ brine reservoir, not the evaporation ponds or DLE plant.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lithium-bearing continental brine (dissolved Li+, typically ~200-2000+ mg/L Li)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Hosts most of the world's economically recoverable lithium (Lithium Triangle: Chile/Atacama, Argentina, Bolivia; also China/Tibet-Qinghai). Solar evaporation ponds and DLE are ROUTE concentration steps, not the origin.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Reservoir = origin; concentrated liquor/pond brine is a route intermediate.

starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium co-produced with geothermal heat/power; brine also carries Mn, Zn, etc.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The deep hot subsurface geothermal reservoir where lithium is dissolved in high-temperature brine (e.g., Salton Sea KGRA, California). Anchored at the geothermal reservoir, not the power plant or DLE recovery unit.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lithium-bearing geothermal brine (dissolved Li+ in hot saline geothermal fluid)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Distinct from continental salar brine: high temperature, tied to geothermal power generation, DLE recovered from spent brine after energy extraction. Salton Sea estimated ~18 Mt Li. Materially different extraction capability -> separate group.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Reservoir = origin; spent brine post-power-generation is a route step.

starting_boundaries.occurrence_type: Companion/byproduct deposit (byproduct of oil & gas produced water)
starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium as byproduct of hydrocarbon extraction; hosted in formation brines (e.g., Smackover Formation, Marcellus)
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The subsurface hydrocarbon-bearing sedimentary formation whose connate/formation brine carries dissolved lithium (e.g., Smackover Formation, Arkansas). Anchored at the formation, not the produced-water DLE plant.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lithium-bearing oilfield formation / produced-water brine (dissolved Li+ co-produced with oil & gas)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Distinct host system: brine co-produced with hydrocarbons, recovered via DLE from produced water. Smackover Formation and Marcellus shale are active development targets. Separate extraction capability -> separate group.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Formation = origin; produced water at surface is a route intermediate.

starting_boundaries.host_source_name: Volcano-sedimentary lithium claystone deposit (smectite/illite; e.g., McDermitt caldera)
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The in-situ lacustrine claystone/tuffaceous sediment body (typically caldera-lake sediments) where lithium is hosted in clay minerals smectite (hectorite) and illite. Anchored at the claystone deposit.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lithium-bearing claystone / clay ore (lithium hosted in smectite/hectorite and Li-illite; ~0.9-1.8 wt% Li in high-grade illite)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Emerging but well-defined primary host (Thacker Pass/McDermitt caldera, Nevada; Clayton Valley clays). Requires materially different extraction (acid/roast leach of clay) than pegmatite or brine -> separate group. No commercial production yet at scale as of 2026 but defined reserves in construction.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Includes hectorite smectite clay occurrences (magnesium-lithium smectite) under the same clay-host group.

starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The in-situ lacustrine sedimentary basin where lithium is hosted in the borosilicate mineral jadarite (LiNaSiB3O7(OH)), interlayered with tuffs. Anchored at the deposit (Jadar Valley, Serbia — only known jadarite locality).
starting_boundaries.output_form: Jadarite ore (lithium-sodium-borosilicate; lithium co-hosted with boron)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Distinct end-member volcano-sedimentary host with unique mineralogy (jadarite) and Li-B co-product processing, materially different from clay/smectite. Currently the Jadar Project, Serbia. Kept separate from clay claystone group due to distinct ore mineral and B co-product.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Deposit = origin; unique to Serbia at present but classified as a reusable host type.

starting_boundaries.host_source_name: Lithium mine tailings / process residue accumulation (standalone, worked directly)
starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium (residual, in tailings from prior spodumene/mica processing)
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: A legacy tailings pile / residue dump (e.g., low-grade spodumene flotation tailings) that is worked directly as a lithium source in its own right, with no active upstream mine feeding it. The accumulation itself is the origin for that secondary route.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Lithium-bearing tailings / residue (residual Li in spodumene tailings ~ up to ~5% Li2O in flotation-recovered fraction; low-grade bulk)
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Per procedure: a standalone accumulation worked directly is its own origin. A tailings stream generated inside a route currently being mapped is NOT a separate boundary — only pre-existing/legacy accumulations qualify here. Recovery via re-flotation or acid leach are route steps.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Only legacy/standalone accumulations qualify; in-route residues remain route intermediates.

starting_boundaries.host_source_name: End-of-life lithium battery / black mass accumulation (recycled)
starting_boundaries.host_commodity: Lithium (plus Ni, Co, Mn, Cu, graphite) in spent Li-ion batteries and scrap
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor: The accumulation of post-consumer and post-industrial spent lithium-ion batteries and manufacturing scrap. Anchored at the collected end-of-life battery / scrap accumulation. Black mass (shredded, thermally treated concentrate) is a ROUTE intermediate downstream of this accumulation.
starting_boundaries.output_form: Spent lithium-ion batteries / manufacturing scrap (lithium hosted in cathode active material within cells); intermediate route form: black mass
starting_boundaries.recovery_note: Distinct EOL host accumulation; hydrometallurgical/pyrometallurgical recovery of Li (as Li2CO3/LiOH) from black mass are route steps. Growing secondary source. Black mass itself is anchored as a route step, not the origin, per anchoring rule.
starting_boundaries.original_source_anchor_note: Origin = the EOL battery/scrap accumulation; black mass is the direct recovery point (a route step), not the origin.

ending_boundaries.description: Dominant marketed lithium chemical; white powder. Sold as technical grade (glass/ceramics/industrial) and battery grade (higher purity, low iron). Same-layer grade variants (technical vs battery) are ONE output form, not separate ending boundaries. Corresponds to child node 'Lithium carbonate' (intermediate material). Function: battery cathode precursor (LFP, standard NMC), glass/ceramic flux, pharma API. Downstream child input form = lithium carbonate.

White crystalline compound; sold as technical grade (greases, industrial) and battery grade (high-nickel NMC/NCA cathodes). Technical vs battery grade are same-layer variants of one output form. Corresponds to child node 'Lithium hydroxide monohydrate' (intermediate material). Function: high-nickel cathode precursor, lithium-soap grease thickener. Downstream child input form = lithium hydroxide monohydrate.

Refined metallic lithium (ingot/foil/granular), produced mainly by molten-salt electrolysis of lithium chloride. Corresponds to child node 'Lithium metal' (intermediate material). Function: Li-metal/solid-state anodes, Al-Li alloys, organolithium/pharma reagents. Classification carried at LOWER (medium) confidence because it is both a distinct processed commercial object (favoring child/output form) and the raw element in metallic form (favoring output-form-only) per the output-form-vs-child rule. Downstream child input form = lithium metal.
